questions.question: The domain of the function f(x) = √(x − 5) + 1/(x − 2) is:
questions.explanation: For √(x−5), we need x − 5 ≥ 0, so x ≥ 5. For 1/(x−2), we need x ≠ 2. Since x ≥ 5 already excludes x = 2, the domain is [5, ∞).

questions.question: The value of cos⁻¹(cos(7π/6)) is:
questions.explanation: cos(7π/6) = cos(π + π/6) = −cos(π/6) = −√3/2. Since cos⁻¹(x) returns values in [0, π], cos⁻¹(−√3/2) = 5π/6.

questions.question: If A is a 3 × 2 matrix and B is a 2 × 3 matrix, then the order of the matrix (AB)^T is:
questions.explanation: A is 3×2 and B is 2×3. The product AB is a 3×3 matrix. The transpose of a 3×3 matrix is also 3×3.

questions.explanation: f'(x) = (1/cos x) · (−sin x) = −tan x. At x = π/4, f'(π/4) = −tan(π/4) = −1.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 5 is increasing on which interval?
The value of ∫ sec²x dx equals:
questions.explanation: This is a standard integral: ∫sec²x dx = tan x + C.

questions.question: The value of ∫₀^π cos x dx equals:
questions.explanation: ∫₀^π cos x dx = [sin x]₀^π = sin(π) − sin(0) = 0 − 0 = 0.

questions.question: The order of the differential equation d²y/dx² + 3(dy/dx)⁴ + y³ = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The order of a differential equation is the order of the highest derivative present. Here, the highest derivative is d²y/dx², so the order is 2.

questions.question: The unit vector in the direction of the vector a = 2i − j + 2k is:
The direction ratios of the line given by (x − 1)/2 = (y + 3)/(−1) = z/4 are:
questions.explanation: The direction ratios are the coefficients in the denominators: (2, −1, 4).

questions.question: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. The probability that it is either a heart or a king is:
In linear programming, the feasible region defined by x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, and x + y ≤ 6 is a:
questions.explanation: The constraints x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 6 form a triangle with vertices (0,0), (6,0), and (0,6).

questions.question: The trace of the 3 × 3 identity matrix I₃ equals:
questions.explanation: The trace is the sum of diagonal elements. For I₃, diagonal entries are all 1, so trace = 1+1+1 = 3.

questions.question: If A is a 3 × 3 skew-symmetric matrix, then the determinant of A equals:
questions.explanation: For a skew-symmetric matrix of odd order, |A| = |A^T| = |−A| = (−1)^n|A|. With n=3, |A| = −|A|, so |A| = 0.

questions.question: For x > 0, tan⁻¹(x) + tan⁻¹(1/x) equals:
questions.explanation: For x > 0, tan⁻¹(x) + tan⁻¹(1/x) = π/2. This is a standard identity.

questions.question: The projection of vector a = 3i + 4j on vector b = i (the x-axis unit vector) equals:
questions.explanation: Projection of a on b = (a·b)/|b| = (3·1 + 4·0)/1 = 3.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. The probability of getting exactly one head equals:
The slope of the normal to the curve y = x² at the point (2, 4) is:
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x. At x = 2, slope of tangent = 4. Slope of normal = −1/(slope of tangent) = −1/4.

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[2, 0], [1, 3]], then the (2,1) entry of the product AB equals:
The value of the determinant |1 2 3; 0 3 1; 0 0 2| equals:
questions.explanation: This is an upper triangular matrix. The determinant is the product of diagonal entries: 1 × 3 × 2 = 6.

If y = e^(x²) · sin x, then dy/dx equals:
options: A) e^(x²)(2x sin x + cos x)
B) e^(x²)(2x sin x − cos x)
C) e^(x²)(x² sin x + cos x)
D) e^(x²)(2x cos x + sin x)
questions.explanation: Using product rule: dy/dx = e^(x²)·2x·sin x + e^(x²)·cos x = e^(x²)(2x sin x + cos x).

questions.question: If y = x³ · ln x, then d²y/dx² equals:
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² ln x + x³ · (1/x) = 3x² ln x + x². d²y/dx² = 6x ln x + 3x² · (1/x) + 2x = 6x ln x + 3x + 2x = 6x ln x + 5x.

questions.question: The value of ∫ x · e^(2x) dx equals:
questions.explanation: Using integration by parts with u = x, dv = e^(2x)dx: ∫x·e^(2x)dx = x·(e^(2x)/2) − ∫(e^(2x)/2)dx = (x/2)e^(2x) − (1/4)e^(2x) + C = (x/2 − 1/4)e^(2x) + C.

questions.question: The value of ∫₀¹ x² · (x³ + 1)^4 dx equals:
The area bounded by the curve y = x² + 1, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 equals:
The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = y² · x is:
questions.explanation: Separating variables: dy/y² = x dx. Integrating: −1/y = x²/2 + C. So y = −1/(x²/2 + C).

questions.question: If a = i + 2j − k and b = 2i − j + 3k, then a × b equals:
The angle between the vectors a = 2i + j − k and b = i − j + 2k is:
The equation of the line passing through the point (1, −2, 3) and parallel to the vector 2i + j − k is:
questions.explanation: The symmetric form of a line through (x₁,y₁,z₁) with direction ratios (a,b,c) is (x−x₁)/a = (y−y₁)/b = (z−z₁)/c. Here: (x−1)/2 = (y+2)/1 = (z−3)/(−1).

questions.question: In a class, 60% of students are boys and 40% are girls. 20% of boys and 30% of girls wear glasses. If a student is chosen at random and found to wear glasses, the probability that the student is a girl equals:
questions.explanation: P(boy) = 0.6, P(girl) = 0.4. P(glasses|boy) = 0.2, P(glasses|girl) = 0.3. P(glasses) = 0.6·0.2 + 0.4·0.3 = 0.12 + 0.12 = 0.24. P(girl|glasses) = P(glasses|girl)·P(girl)/P(glasses) = 0.12/0.24 = 1/2.

questions.question: A factory has two machines A and B. Machine A produces 40% of items with 5% defective. Machine B produces 60% of items with 3% defective. An item is selected at random and found to be defective. The probability it was produced by machine A equals:
Maximize Z = 2x + 3y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 8, 2x + y ≤ 10. The maximum value of Z equals:
questions.explanation: Corner points: (0,0)→Z=0, (5,0)→Z=10, (0,8)→Z=24. Intersection of x+y=8 and 2x+y=10: x=2, y=6, Z=2·2+3·6=4+18=22. Maximum Z = 24 at (0,8).

questions.question: The derivative of f(x) = sin⁻¹(3x − 4x³) for x ∈ (−1/2, 1/2) is:
questions.explanation: Note that 3x − 4x³ = sin(3θ) where x = sin θ. For x ∈ (−1/2, 1/2), f(x) = 3 sin⁻¹x. So f'(x) = 3/√(1−x²).

questions.question: If y = (sin x)^x, then dy/dx equals:
options: A) (sin x)^x [ln(sin x) + x tan x]
B) (sin x)^x [ln(sin x) − x cot x]
D) (sin x)^x [ln(sin x) + x cot x]
questions.explanation: ln y = x · ln(sin x). (1/y)dy/dx = ln(sin x) + x · (1/sin x) · cos x = ln(sin x) + x cot x. dy/dx = y[ln(sin x) + x cot x] = (sin x)^x [ln(sin x) + x cot x].

questions.question: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = (x² + y²)/(2xy) is:
questions.explanation: This is a homogeneous equation. Let y = vx, then dy/dx = v + x(dv/dx). Substituting: v + x(dv/dx) = (1 + v²)/(2v). So x(dv/dx) = (1−v²)/(2v). Separating: 2v/(1−v²)dv = dx/x. Integrating: −ln|1−v²| = ln|x| + C. So x²−y² = Cx.

The eigenvalues of the matrix A = [[3, 1], [2, 2]] are:
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation: |A − λI| = 0. |3−λ, 1; 2, 2−λ| = (3−λ)(2−λ) − 2 = λ² − 5λ + 4 = 0. (λ−1)(λ−4) = 0. Eigenvalues: λ = 1, 4.

questions.question: The shortest distance between the skew lines L₁: r = i + j + λ(i + j + k) and L₂: r = 2i + j − k + μ(i + 2j + 2k) is:
questions.explanation: L₁ passes through a₁ = i+j with direction b₁ = i+j+k. L₂ passes through a₂ = 2i+j−k with direction b₂ = i+2j+2k. a₂−a₁ = i−k. b₁×b₂ = |i j k; 1 1 1; 1 2 2| = i(2−2) − j(2−1) + k(2−1) = [0,−1,1]. |b₁×b₂| = √2. Shortest distance = |(a₂−a₁)·(b₁×b₂)|/|b₁×b₂| = |[1,0,−1]·[0,−1,1]|/√2 = |0+0−1|/√2 = 1/√2.

questions.question: A ladder 13 m long leans against a vertical wall. If the bottom slides away from the wall at 2 m/s, how fast is the angle between the ladder and the ground changing when the bottom is 5 m from the wall?
questions.explanation: Let x be distance from wall, θ be angle with ground. cos θ = x/13. Differentiating: −sin θ · dθ/dt = (1/13)·dx/dt. When x = 5, sin θ = 12/13, dx/dt = 2. −(12/13)·dθ/dt = 2/13. dθ/dt = −2/12 = −1/6 rad/s.

questions.question: The value of ∫₀^π x · sin x dx equals:
questions.explanation: Using integration by parts with u = x, dv = sin x dx: ∫x sin x dx = −x cos x + ∫cos x dx = −x cos x + sin x. Evaluating from 0 to π: [−π·(−1) + 0] − [0 + 0] = π.

questions.question: The particular solution of dy/dx + y tan x = sec x with y(0) = 1 is:
options: A) y = x sin x + cos x
B) y = sin x + cos x
C) y = sin x − cos x
D) y = sin x + x cos x
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: e^(∫tan x dx) = e^(−ln cos x) = sec x. Multiplying: sec x · dy/dx + sec x · tan x · y = sec²x. d/dx(y · sec x) = sec²x. Integrating: y · sec x = tan x + C. y = sin x + C cos x. Using y(0) = 1: 1 = 0 + C·1, so C = 1. Thus y = sin x + cos x.

questions.question: If X follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2, then P(X ≥ 1) equals:
questions.explanation: For Poisson with λ = 2: P(X ≥ 1) = 1 − P(X = 0) = 1 − e⁻² · 2⁰/0! = 1 − e⁻².

questions.question: The equation of the plane that passes through the point (1, 2, 3) and contains the line of intersection of the planes x + y + z = 6 and 2x + 3y + 4z = 10 is:
questions.explanation: The family of planes through the line of intersection is: (x+y+z−6) + λ(2x+3y+4z−10) = 0. For the plane to pass through (1,2,3): (1+2+3−6) + λ(2+6+12−10) = 0 + 10λ = 0, so λ = 0. The plane is x + y + z = 6.

Using the property ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a−x) dx, the value of ∫₀^(π/2) (sin x)/(sin x + cos x) dx equals:
questions.explanation: Let I = ∫₀^(π/2) (sin x)/(sin x + cos x) dx. Using the property: I = ∫₀^(π/2) (sin(π/2−x))/(sin(π/2−x) + cos(π/2−x)) dx = ∫₀^(π/2) (cos x)/(cos x + sin x) dx. Adding the two expressions: 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) (sin x + cos x)/(sin x + cos x) dx = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2. So I = π/4.
